{{nihongo|'''Kukumiohiko Shrine'''|久久美雄彦神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

'''Kukumiohiko Shrine''' (くくみおひこじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Yōrō, Gifu|Q153814|qid=Q153814}}, {{ill|Yōrō District, Gifu|Q1155060|qid=Q1155060}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}. It is the Kukumiohiko Shrine of {{ill|Tagi district|Q11431050|qid=Q11431050}} in {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. It is also written as Kugumiohiko Shrine.

It stands along the {{ill|Tōkai Nature Trail|Q4249812|qid=Q4249812}}, on the mid-slope near the northern end of the {{ill|Yōrō Mountains|Q8062668|qid=Q8062668}}.

=== History ===
The founding period is unknown. Because the ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}'' records that it received the divine rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade in {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 5 ({{ill|838|Q23838|qid=Q23838}}) from {{ill|Emperor Ninmyō|Q349271|qid=Q349271}}, it is presumed to have been founded no later than the early {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292}}.

There are records that during the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}} it was called Kugumihohiko Daimyōjin, and in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was called Kugumiohiko Jinja Daimyōjin. When it became a gōsha in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was renamed Kukumiohiko Shrine.

=== Enshrined deity ===
*Kukumiohiko-no-Kami
:What kind of deity Kukumiohiko-no-Kami is remains unclear. The following theories exist:
#The same deity as Tatamihiko-no-Mikoto of {{ill|Ibuki Shrine|Q11379321|qid=Q11379321}}. However, deities of Ibuki Shrine also have multiple theories, including {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamata no Orochi}}, {{ill|Amenohoakari|fr|Ame-no-hoakari|it|Amenohoakari|ja|天火明命|ko|아메노호아카리|mni|ꯑꯃꯦꯅꯣꯍꯣꯑꯀꯔꯤ|simple|Ame-no-hoakari|zh|天火明命|qid=Q10940411}}, and {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|qid=Q1373935|lt=Kusayafugō-no-Mikoto}}; Tatamihiko-no-Mikoto (also called Ebisudake-no-Kami, Kibuki-no-O-no-Kami, or Ibuki-no-Kami) is regarded as the deity of {{ill|Mount Ibuki|Q2624360|qid=Q2624360}}.
#Kukumihohiko-no-Kami, a divided deity of Ama-no-Tobeno-Mikoto. Details of Ama-no-Tobeno-Mikoto are unknown, but it is presumed to be {{ill|Otonoji and Otonobe|Q11073597|qid=Q11073597|lt=Ōtobe-no-Mikoto}}.
